title: Maxims
author: François de La Rochefoucauld
translator: J. W. Willis Bund & J. Hain Friswell, 1871 (public domain, Project Gutenberg #9105)
blurb: A French duke's razor-sharp one-liners about vanity, self-interest and the hidden motives behind our 'virtues'.

self-love.e: Self-love made him fish for compliments.

disinterestedness.e: Her disinterestedness made her a fair judge.

hypocrisy.m: Pretending to have virtues you don't have.
hypocrisy.e: Preaching saving money while splurging is hypocrisy.

homage.e: The crowd paid homage to the old singer.

misfortunes.e: Their misfortunes included a flood and a fire.

cards.title: Self-interest speaks every language
cards.text: Self-interest can pretend to be anything — even someone who cares nothing for gain.
cards.quote: Interest speaks all sorts of tongues and plays all sorts of characters; even that of disinterestedness.
cards.qMean: Self-interest can disguise itself as anything, even generosity.
cards.qLife: A 'free' trial that quietly turns into a monthly charge.

cards.title: Others' troubles are light
cards.text: We all have plenty of strength to bear other people's misfortunes.
cards.quote: We have all sufficient strength to support the misfortunes of others.
cards.qMean: It's easy to be brave about other people's problems.
cards.qLife: Telling a friend 'it's just a breakup, you'll be fine.'
cards.cap: Abraham Bosse - Graveurs en taille-douce · public domain

cards.title: Hypocrisy pays respect
cards.text: When people fake virtue, they admit that virtue is valuable.
cards.quote: Hypocrisy is the homage vice pays to virtue.
cards.qMean: Pretending to be good shows that even bad people respect goodness.
cards.qLife: A polluting company adding green leaves to its logo.
cards.cap: Illustration for Molière's Tartuffe · public domain

cards.title: Promises and fears
cards.text: We promise according to our hopes and deliver according to our fears.
cards.quote: We promise according to our hopes; we perform according to our fears.
cards.qMean: We promise big when hopeful, and do less when afraid.
cards.qLife: Promising to finish the project in a week, then delivering half because of worry.
cards.cap: Van der Meulen, Louis XIV and his court · public domain

cards.title: The best flatterer
cards.text: Nobody flatters you as well as your own self-love.
cards.quote: Self-love is the greatest of flatterers.
cards.qMean: Your own vanity praises you more than anyone else does.
cards.qLife: Thinking you sang perfectly until you hear the recording.
cards.cap: Unknown French Master - Allegory of the Vanity of Earthly Things - 2 · public domain

cards.title: Never as happy or sad
cards.text: We are never as happy or as unhappy as we imagine.
cards.quote: We are never so happy or so unhappy as we suppose.
cards.qMean: Good and bad times are rarely as extreme as they feel.
cards.qLife: The rejection that felt like the end turned out to be a small bump.
cards.cap: The Triumph of Fortune · public domain
